newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal's Sonae wins plaudits for split.
newsitem.headline: Portugal's Sonae wins plaudits for split.

text.p: Shares in retailer and real estate group Sonae Investimentos look set to climb after the splitting off of the group's industrial interests, analysts said.

Analyst Jose Freire of Espirito Santo Research sees net profit, excluding extraordinaries, rising to around 11 billion escudos in 1997 from a forecast eight billion last year. Sonae posts its 1996 results on March 17.

The share price, which was up nearly two percent at 5,806 escudos on Tuesday, was seen hitting 6,300-6,400 escudos by the end of the year in a recent research note circulated to clients by Banco Portugues de Investimento.
Analysts saw 6,000 as a short-term goal.

"The split is showing itself to be beneficial for Sonae Investimentos' shareholders," said Freire. "Sales will be down just 2.5 percent (despite the split), but profit will rise 37 percent without including extraordinaries."

After the reorganisation, which took effect at the start of the year, although rights to the new company Inparsa were only split from Sonae Investimentos' stock this week, Sonae business will focus almost entirely on retail with some real estate.

"We believe that Sonae Investimentos (stock) still has some growth potential because...from now on it is a simpler company, a retailer which deserves to be on multiples closer to (retailer) Jeronimo Martins and other international companies," said Joao Vermelho of Central de Investimentos.
"We are going to see Sonae go rapidly above 6,000 escudos," he added.
Freire pointed to Sonae's potential for expansion in Brazil in the building and management of shopping centres as well as in retailing.
The Portuguese retail sector is also seen as positive overall. Even if it is slightly more expensive than Spain, its growth possibilities are greater, analysts say.

"Portuguese retailers are in a phase of geographic diversification. Jeronimo Martins is in Eastern Europe and Sonae in Brasil, ensuring some growth in sales and results into the next century," said Vermelho.
Paulo Guerreiro of brokers M.Valores predicted a price earnings ratio for Sonae Investimentos and Jeronimo Martins of 22 in 1997, against the average 21 in Spain.
Jose Carlos Tomas of BPI saw a p/e of 25 in 1997 and 20 in 1998, on the basis of profits before extraodinaries of nine and 12 billion escudos in the two years.
Freire expected Sonae's profits to rise to 13.8 billion escudos in 1998 from sales of 554.5 billion, against 448.65 billion in the current year.

The analyst saw the dividend yield easing to 3.2 percent this year from an expected 4.2 percent in 1996 with the gross dividend rising to 175 escudos from the 160 escudos the company is forecast to pay for 1996.
Guerreiro predicted a net profit in 1997, excluding extraordinaries of 7.6 billion escudos and nine billion in 1998.
